title: Self-Hosted Model Evaluation, Capacity, and Observability
summary: Join exact-build quality and safety evaluation, representative load, bounded capacity, privacy-conscious telemetry, cost, and actionable alerts.
prerequisites: A versioned serving-unit manifest and bounded workload claim
Representative routine, important-slice, boundary, adversarial, and failure cases
Service objectives, capacity and cost owners, and a telemetry data policy

sections.title: Evaluate the exact serving build and declared claim
paragraphs: Bind every result to model and tokenizer digests, runtime or image, drivers and execution provider, templates, adapters, gateway, policy, configuration, tool set, evaluation dataset, grader configuration, and time. Predeclare the intended workload, prohibited effects, important slices, metrics, thresholds, critical gates, and human release authority before observing the candidate.

Use deterministic graders for schemas, citations, authorization, limits, tool arguments, and terminal postconditions where possible. Use calibrated blinded human review for usefulness, nuance, accessibility, and consequential judgment. A separately configured model-assisted reviewer can add a versioned signal only after calibration and disagreement analysis; it cannot be the sole judge or release authority.

sections.title: Measure capacity, telemetry, and cost together
paragraphs: Drive the real gateway with a representative distribution of body size, context, output, concurrency, burst, cancellation, timeout, malformed, overload, dependency, and recovery cases. Report latency and first-output distributions, queue time, throughput, rejection and error rates, resource saturation, warm-up, placement, replica behavior, and attributable cost. Issue limits for request, context, output, rate, concurrency, queue, deadline, retry, resources, and budget.

Start telemetry design from operator questions. Correlate secret-safe logs, metrics, and traces across request, policy, gateway, exact build, infrastructure, evaluation reference, cost, and terminal outcome. Control content capture, cardinality, sampling, access, retention, and deletion. Test alert routing, grouping, suppression, runbook action, recovery condition, and telemetry loss so a silent monitoring failure cannot look like a healthy service.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the exact build and claim, versioned cases and slices, grader calibration, case and slice results, critical-gate disposition, representative load profile, distributions and saturation, capacity and cost decision, telemetry data contract, end-to-end correlation, alert and telemetry-loss tests, human approval, owners, residual risks, and expiry or next review date.

Stop release or admission on a critical slice or prohibited effect, uncontrolled queue or saturation, telemetry disclosure or blindness, cost-limit breach, or missing human authority. Hold the candidate, reduce or stop exposure, preserve minimal secret-free evidence, restore the known-good build and operating limits, and verify quality, safety, capacity, alerts, cost, and postconditions before reopening.

sections.title: Evidence status and interpretation
paragraphs: The request rows, metrics, costs, thresholds, expected outputs, and alert records in this supplement are fictional classroom values. They are not measurements from a local machine, gateway, model server, collector, or production deployment.

The Python output is proposed expected output that can be independently reproduced. This artifact does not claim that the scripts were executed while drafting. An actual local observation would require an execution record containing the command, Python version, exact files and digests, standard output, standard error, exit status, host or runner identity, and observation time.

Deployment qualification is UNKNOWN. Establishing it requires authorized testing of the exact serving build under a representative real workload, calibrated grading, capacity and cost evidence, telemetry and alert verification, human approval, and an expiry or review date.

sections.title: Completed fictional instance and predeclared decision policy
paragraphs: The fictional serving-unit identity is build build-2026-09-20-a; model digest sha256:model-a; tokenizer digest sha256:tokenizer-a; runtime image registry.example.invalid/inference@sha256:image-a; driver digest sha256:driver-a; provider provider-neutral; template template-7; adapter adapter-none; gateway gateway-3; policy policy-12; configuration config-41; tools toolset-2; evaluation dataset eval-2026-09-20-v1; and grader configuration grader-5. These are classroom identifiers, not real registry references.

Before inspecting the fixture, the policy declares a two-second window, exact-build enforcement, successful-request nearest-rank p95 latency at most 0.85 seconds, successful-case quality pass rate at least 0.85, important-slice pass rate at least 0.95, maximum queue time at most 0.25 seconds, total attributable cost at most 0.120 fictional cost units, telemetry completeness exactly 1.00, at most one timeout, zero terminal errors, at most one overload rejection, zero prohibited effects, and required human release authority. The important-slice, prohibited-effect, telemetry, queue, cost, and human-authority checks are critical gates.

The completed fixture contains ten arrivals: eight successes, one timeout, zero terminal errors, and one overload rejection. Seven of eight successful requests pass the quality grader. The important slice contains two successful requests, only one of which passes. There are no recorded prohibited effects, but human release authority is absent.

The computed aggregate metrics are a 0.45-second average successful latency, 0.80-second nearest-rank successful p95, 5.00 arrivals per second, 4.00 successful completions per second, 0.100 timeout rate, 0.000 terminal-error rate, 0.100 rejection rate, 0.875 overall successful-case quality, 0.500 important-slice quality, 0.20-second maximum queue time, 0.101 total cost, and 1.000 telemetry completeness.

The result is HOLD because the important-slice gate fails and required human authority is absent. This disposition is computed from gate results, not printed as a constant. Attractive aggregate latency, queue, cost, and overall-quality values cannot override a failed critical slice.

The fixture does not cover cancellation, malformed input, dependency failure, recovery, sustained load, varied placement, or replica transitions.

Permissions: classroom data and offline standard-library calculation are permitted. Real model invocation, gateway load, production telemetry access, model-assisted review, spending, and release authorization are not evidenced. Human release authority is recorded as false.

The fixture does not substitute for calibrated blinded human review of usefulness, nuance, accessibility, or consequential judgment.

The intended allowlist is build_id, route_class, provider_family, slice_id, result_class, status_class, and bounded infrastructure classes. Raw prompts, completions, secrets, tokens, user identifiers, and unbounded request parameters are excluded from ordinary metrics and logs.

Verification: independently run analyzer.py and evaluation_fixture.py, then run changed_task.py, changed_answer.py, and test_analyzer.py in that order. Compare exact output, inspect failed-gate reasons, and preserve the files and execution record. This verifies classroom arithmetic only.

sections.title: Reusable functional analyzer
paragraphs: Save this file first as analyzer.py. It uses only the Python 3.11 standard library. It performs no network access, temporary-file operations, or deletion. Decimal is used for input conversion, arithmetic, thresholds, rates, and percentile values.

Validation rejects an empty dataset, mixed build IDs, duplicate request IDs, missing required fields, unknown status, non-Boolean grading, telemetry, or prohibited-effect markers, nonfinite or negative latency, queue, or cost, and zero, negative, or nonfinite duration. It rejects missing policy fields; nonfinite or out-of-range rate thresholds; a telemetry requirement other than exactly 1.00; nonfinite or negative latency, queue, or cost limits; Boolean, fractional, or negative count ceilings; and non-Boolean human authority. It also rejects an absent predeclared important slice instead of dividing by zero.
A telemetry marker of false is a valid observation of telemetry loss. It therefore reaches gate evaluation and causes a telemetry gate failure. A missing telemetry field is structurally invalid.

sections.title: Baseline fixture and concrete run procedure
paragraphs: Save the following as evaluation_fixture.py in the same directory as analyzer.py. Run python3.11 analyzer.py first to confirm it imports without error, then run python3.11 evaluation_fixture.py. Running analyzer.py alone intentionally produces no output.

The observations represent terminal outcomes recorded within the fictional two-second window. Therefore ten divided by two is labeled arrival rate, while eight successes divided by two is labeled successful-completion throughput. A timeout is not relabeled as an error, and a rejection is not combined with either category.

code.label: evaluation_fixture.py
code.code:
from decimal import Decimal
from analyzer import analyze

BUILD = 'build-2026-09-20-a'
DURATION = Decimal('2.0')
POLICY = {
    'exact_build': BUILD,
    'p95_max': '0.85',
    'quality_min': '0.85',
    'important_slice': 'important',
    'important_min': '0.95',
    'queue_max': '0.25',
    'cost_max': '0.120',
    'telemetry_min': '1.00',
    'max_timeouts': 1,
    'max_errors': 0,
    'max_rejections': 1,
    'max_prohibited_effects': 0,
    'human_authority': False,
}


def observations():
    values = [
        ('r01', 'routine', 'success', '0.10', '0.00', '0.010', True, True, False),
        ('r02', 'routine', 'success', '0.20', '0.05', '0.012', True, True, False),
        ('r03', 'routine', 'success', '0.30', '0.10', '0.011', True, True, False),
        ('r04', 'routine', 'success', '0.40', '0.10', '0.013', True, True, False),
        ('r05', 'routine', 'success', '0.50', '0.15', '0.009', True, True, False),
        ('r06', 'routine', 'success', '0.60', '0.15', '0.010', True, True, False),
        ('r07', 'important', 'success', '0.70', '0.20', '0.014', True, True, False),
        ('r08', 'important', 'success', '0.80', '0.20', '0.015', False, True, False),
        ('r09', 'boundary', 'timeout', '0.00', '0.10', '0.004', False, True, False),
        ('r10', 'overload', 'rejected', '0.00', '0.20', '0.003', False, True, False),
    ]
    names = ('request_id', 'slice_id', 'status', 'latency', 'queue', 'cost',
             'quality_pass', 'telemetry', 'prohibited_effect')
    return [dict(zip(names, value), build_id=BUILD) for value in values]


def main():
    result = analyze(observations(), DURATION, POLICY)
    m = result['metrics']
    print(f'build={result["build_id"]}')
    print(f'arrivals={m["arrivals"]} success={m["successes"]} timeout={m["timeouts"]} error={m["errors"]} rejected={m["rejections"]}')
    print(f'arrival_rate={m["arrival_rate"]:.2f}/s successful_completion_throughput={m["successful_completion_throughput"]:.2f}/s')
    print(f'timeout_rate={m["timeout_rate"]:.3f} error_rate={m["error_rate"]:.3f} rejection_rate={m["rejection_rate"]:.3f}')
    print(f'average_success_latency={m["average_success_latency"]:.2f}s p95_success_latency={m["p95_success_latency"]:.2f}s')
    print(f'overall_quality_pass={m["quality_pass_rate"]:.3f} important_slice_pass={m["important_pass_rate"]:.3f}')
    print(f'max_queue={m["max_queue"]:.2f}s cost={m["cost"]:.3f} telemetry_completeness={m["telemetry_completeness"]:.3f}')
    print('gates=' + ','.join(f'{name}:{passed}' for name, passed in result['gates'].items()))
    print(f'decision={result["decision"]} reasons={",".join(result["reasons"]) or "none"}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

sections.title: Baseline expected output and diagnosed failure
paragraphs: The exact expected output is shown below. It is a reproducible prediction from the supplied fixture, not a claim of actual execution.

The nearest-rank p95 index is ceiling of 0.95 times 8, which is 8, so the p95 is 0.80 seconds. The aggregate quality rate is 7 divided by 8, or 0.875. The important-slice rate is 1 divided by 2, or 0.500.

The causal release diagnosis is that important_slice is false because 0.500 is below 0.950, and human_authority is false because approval was not supplied. The analyzer derives HOLD by checking whether any gate is false.

The original flawed record described ten divided by two as throughput and combined the timeout and rejection into errors=2. The correction labels 5.00 per second as arrival rate, reports successful-completion throughput as 4.00 per second, and reports timeout=1, error=0, and rejected=1 separately.

sections.title: Independent changed answer and causal grading feedback
paragraphs: After completing the starter independently, save the full answer below as changed_answer.py. Run python3.11 changed_answer.py. It imports the same analyzer but declares its own independent fixture and policy.

The answer computes a 0.50-second p95, 6.00 arrivals per second, 5.00 successful completions per second, 0.800 successful-case quality, one timeout, and 0.833 telemetry completeness. The decision is not hardcoded. It becomes HOLD because quality, timeout, and telemetry gates are false.

Causal grading feedback: p95 passes because ceiling of 0.95 times 5 is 5 and the fifth ordered successful latency is 0.50. Quality fails because four of five successes pass, which is 0.800 rather than at least 0.950. The no-timeout requirement fails because c06 timed out. Telemetry fails because only five of six arrivals have telemetry, yielding 0.833 when formatted to three decimal places.
A response that reports only p95 and the six-arrival rate is incomplete. It must distinguish 6.00 arrivals per second from 5.00 successful completions per second and apply every changed gate.

sections.title: Meaningful positive, gate-failure, and rejection tests
paragraphs: Save the following as test_analyzer.py after saving the other four files. Run python3.11 test_analyzer.py. The test helper raises AssertionError if invalid input is silently accepted, so a broken validator cannot make a rejection test disappear without failing the test program.

The 16-test-group suite includes a positive fixture that passes the original 0.95 important-slice threshold by changing r08 to a passing measurement and supplying Boolean human authority. Each group can contain multiple assertions or loop-generated cases. It separately covers an isolated important-slice failure, telemetry loss, a prohibited-effect gate failure, mixed build, duplicate ID, missing fields, malformed row Booleans, malformed authority, nonfinite and negative numeric values, empty samples, invalid durations, unknown status, invalid policy rates and limits, and invalid count ceilings.
The telemetry-loss case is a valid analyzed record and must produce HOLD with telemetry in its reasons. Structural and numeric corruption cases must raise ValueError.

code.label: test_analyzer.py
code.code:
from decimal import Decimal
from analyzer import analyze
from evaluation_fixture import observations, POLICY, DURATION


def passing_policy():
    policy = dict(POLICY)
    policy['human_authority'] = True
    return policy


def passing_observations():
    rows = observations()
    next(row for row in rows if row['request_id'] == 'r08')['quality_pass'] = True
    return rows


def assert_invalid(label, rows, duration=DURATION, policy=None):
    selected_policy = POLICY if policy is None else policy
    try:
        analyze(rows, duration, selected_policy)
    except ValueError:
        return
    raise AssertionError(f'{label}: invalid input was accepted')


def run_tests():
    count = 0

    result = analyze(passing_observations(), DURATION, passing_policy())
    assert result['decision'] == 'PASS' and not result['reasons']
    assert result['metrics']['important_pass_rate'] == Decimal('1')
    assert passing_policy()['important_min'] == POLICY['important_min'] == '0.95'
    count += 1

    policy = dict(POLICY)
    policy['human_authority'] = True
    result = analyze(observations(), DURATION, policy)
    assert result['decision'] == 'HOLD'
    assert result['reasons'] == ['important_slice']
    count += 1

    rows = passing_observations()
    rows[0]['telemetry'] = False
    result = analyze(rows, DURATION, passing_policy())
    assert result['decision'] == 'HOLD' and result['reasons'] == ['telemetry']
    count += 1

    rows = passing_observations()
    rows[0]['prohibited_effect'] = True
    result = analyze(rows, DURATION, passing_policy())
    assert result['decision'] == 'HOLD'
    assert result['reasons'] == ['prohibited_effect']
    count += 1

    rows = observations()
    del rows[0]['queue']
    assert_invalid('missing_field', rows)
    count += 1

    for field, value in (
        ('quality_pass', 'false'),
        ('telemetry', 1),
        ('prohibited_effect', 'false'),
    ):
        rows = observations()
        rows[0][field] = value
        assert_invalid(f'non_boolean_{field}', rows)
    count += 1

    for value in ('false', 1, None):
        policy = dict(POLICY)
        policy['human_authority'] = value
        assert_invalid('non_boolean_authority', observations(), policy=policy)
    count += 1

    rows = observations()
    rows[0]['build_id'] = 'other-build'
    assert_invalid('mixed_build', rows)
    rows = observations()
    rows[1]['request_id'] = rows[0]['request_id']
    assert_invalid('duplicate_id', rows)
    count += 1

    for field, value in (
        ('latency', Decimal('NaN')),
        ('queue', Decimal('Infinity')),
        ('cost', Decimal('-0.001')),
        ('latency', Decimal('-0.01')),
    ):
        rows = observations()
        rows[0][field] = value
        assert_invalid(f'invalid_{field}_{value}', rows)
    count += 1

    assert_invalid('empty_dataset', [])
    rows = observations()
    for row in rows:
        if row['slice_id'] == 'important':
            row['slice_id'] = 'routine'
    assert_invalid('empty_important_slice', rows)
    count += 1

    for value in (Decimal('0'), Decimal('-1'), Decimal('NaN'), Decimal('Infinity')):
        assert_invalid(f'invalid_duration_{value}', observations(), value)
    count += 1

    rows = observations()
    rows[0]['status'] = 'unknown'
    assert_invalid('unknown_status', rows)
    count += 1

    for field, value in (
        ('quality_min', '-0.01'),
        ('important_min', '1.01'),
        ('telemetry_min', '0.99'),
        ('quality_min', 'NaN'),
    ):
        policy = dict(POLICY)
        policy[field] = value
        assert_invalid(f'invalid_policy_{field}_{value}', observations(), policy=policy)
    count += 1

    for field, value in (
        ('p95_max', '-0.01'),
        ('queue_max', 'Infinity'),
        ('cost_max', '-1'),
    ):
        policy = dict(POLICY)
        policy[field] = value
        assert_invalid(f'invalid_policy_{field}_{value}', observations(), policy=policy)
    count += 1

    for field in ('max_timeouts', 'max_errors', 'max_rejections', 'max_prohibited_effects'):
        for value in (-1, 1.5, True):
            policy = dict(POLICY)
            policy[field] = value
            assert_invalid(f'invalid_count_{field}_{value}', observations(), policy=policy)
    count += 1

    policy = dict(POLICY)
    del policy['quality_min']
    assert_invalid('missing_policy_field', observations(), policy=policy)
    count += 1

    assert count == 16
    print(f'PASS {count} tests')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_tests()

sections.title: Exact filenames, run order, and test output
paragraphs: Place analyzer.py, evaluation_fixture.py, changed_task.py, changed_answer.py, and test_analyzer.py in one ordinary working directory. No system temporary directory is needed. The scripts do not use a network or delete files.

Run, in order: python3.11 analyzer.py; python3.11 evaluation_fixture.py; python3.11 changed_task.py; python3.11 changed_answer.py; python3.11 test_analyzer.py. The first command produces no output if import and syntax checks succeed. The second and fourth commands produce the exact metric outputs shown in their answer sections. The third prints the supplied starter rows and requirements without revealing an answer.

The exact successful test output is shown below. Any traceback, nonzero exit, missing PASS line, or count other than 16 test groups is a failed classroom verification and must be investigated rather than relabeled as success.

sections.title: Telemetry contract and loss handling
paragraphs: Correlate secret-safe logs, metrics, and traces across request, policy, gateway, exact build, infrastructure, evaluation reference, attributable cost, and terminal outcome. Each correlation record should use a non-sensitive request correlation identifier and exact build identifier.

The metrics-label allowlist is build_id, route_class, provider_family, slice_id, result_class, status_class, and bounded region or replica class when operationally necessary. Raw prompts, completions, secrets, authorization tokens, user IDs, exact customer text, and unbounded request parameters are prohibited from ordinary metrics and logs. Content capture, cardinality, sampling, access, retention, and deletion require explicit controls.

OpenTelemetry publishes shared semantic conventions for telemetry naming at https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/. That documentation does not prove that this fictional fixture has an actual collector, exporter, store, access control, retention process, or deletion process.

When telemetry is false for an observed request, the analyzer computes incomplete telemetry and fails the gate. When the telemetry field is absent or malformed, validation rejects the evidence. In an authorized deployment, either condition should trigger the predeclared exposure-reduction or stop procedure rather than appearing healthy.

sections.title: Alert routing, grouping, suppression, and recovery
paragraphs: Completed fictional alert record TelemetryCompletenessLow: trigger below 1.00 for two consecutive evaluation windows; route to capacity and privacy owners; group by build_id and route_class; suppress duplicate child alerts while the parent telemetry-loss incident is active; hold new exposure; preserve minimal secret-safe evidence; inspect collector and exporter health; and recover only after two consecutive complete windows plus a successful end-to-end correlation check.

Completed fictional alert record ImportantSliceGateFailed: route to the evaluation owner and human release authority; group by build_id and slice_id; suppress repeats for the same unchanged incident; preserve failing case references without restricted content; and require corrected evaluation plus human disposition before reopening.

Prometheus Alertmanager documents alert grouping, routing, inhibition, and silencing at https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/. These classroom records are not actual Alertmanager configurations or test results.

Actual verification must apply authorized configuration, send controlled test alerts, observe destinations and grouping, test inhibition and silence behavior, exercise the runbook, confirm recovery notifications, and separately test telemetry-loss detection. Results of those actions are UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Operating limits and required operational follow-up
paragraphs: Before real load, owners must issue limits for request body, context, output, request rate, concurrency, queue, deadline, retry, resources, and budget. The only numeric limits completed here are fictional exercise values. Production values remain UNKNOWN until service owners establish them from representative workloads, service objectives, safety constraints, and cost authority.

Drive the real gateway with representative body sizes, contexts, outputs, concurrency, bursts, cancellations, timeouts, malformed requests, overload, dependency failures, and recovery. Include routine, important, boundary, adversarial, and failure slices. Record first-output and completion latency distributions, queue time, arrival rate, successful-completion throughput, rejection rate, timeout rate, terminal-error rate, saturation, warm-up, placement, replica behavior, and attributable cost.

Calibrate deterministic graders for schemas, citations, authorization, limits, tool arguments, and terminal postconditions. Use calibrated blinded human review for usefulness, nuance, accessibility, and consequential judgment. Record disagreements, reviewer qualifications, versioned grader configuration, critical-gate disposition, and human release authority.

Verify telemetry content controls, cardinality, sampling, access, retention, deletion, end-to-end correlation, alert routing, grouping, suppression, runbook action, recovery, and telemetry-loss detection. A silent monitoring failure must not be interpreted as service health.

Exercise authorized rollout and rollback, preserve minimal secret-safe evidence, restore a known-good serving unit and limits, and repeat quality, safety, capacity, telemetry, alert, and cost checks before reopening. Kubernetes documents Deployment rollout and rollback behavior at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/ and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale/. Those pages do not establish successful local rollback, autoscaling, or safe state migration for this candidate.

The final evidence package must identify exact build and claim, versioned cases and slices, grader calibration, results, failed and passed gates, load profile, distributions, saturation, cost decision, telemetry contract, alert tests, owners, human approval, residual risks, and expiry or next review date. Until that package exists and all critical gates pass, deployment authorization remains UNKNOWN and exposure must remain held.

sections.title: Provider-neutral transfer and authoritative references
paragraphs: The procedure is provider-neutral because it controls observable interfaces and provenance fields: model and tokenizer digests, runtime image, drivers, execution provider, templates, adapters, gateway, policy, configuration, tools, datasets, graders, workload, telemetry contract, and release authority. It does not infer capability, safety, performance, or license terms for an untested artifact family.

NIST publishes the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework at https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework. MLCommons publishes its inference datacenter benchmark information at https://mlcommons.org/benchmarks/inference-datacenter/. SLSA publishes its provenance specification at https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance.

OpenTelemetry semantic conventions are at https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/. Prometheus Alertmanager documentation is at https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/. Kubernetes Deployment and autoscaling documentation is at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/ and https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale/.

These first-party references support general practices for risk management, benchmarking, provenance, telemetry naming, alert handling, rollout, rollback, and autoscaling. They do not establish the fictional metrics, actual execution, real capacity, cost attribution, human approval, or deployment qualification presented here.
